title: A Parallelizable Algorithm for Constrained Maximization of Preferences in Large Time-Dependent Graphs
summary: This paper studies route selection that maximizes preferences such as safety or scenic value while respecting a travel-time limit on time-dependent networks. Its recursive approach reuses intermediate computations and exposes independent work for multicore execution. Evaluation on large road networks examines route quality and runtime relative to existing methods.

title: A User-Configurable Navigation System for Wideness and Turn-Aware Routing
label: Demonstration · Demos and Posters
venue: 27th IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM)
summary: This demonstration presents an interactive navigation system for long or towing vehicles. Users can adjust the balance between road width, difficult turns, and acceptable journey time, then explore alternative routes under changing road conditions. The interface combines preference switching with map-based visualization to make the safety–travel-time trade-off easier to inspect.

title: Interval Based Constrained Path Optimization in Time-Dependent Road Networks
label: WISE 2025 · proceedings published 2026
venue: Web Information Systems Engineering – WISE 2025, Proceedings, Part II
citation: Lecture Notes in Computer Science 16368, pp. 165–176 (published 2026)
summary: This work extends constrained route optimization from a fixed departure time to a departure interval. It seeks a suitable route and departure time together, maximizing a user preference within a travel-time constraint. The algorithm reduces repeated computation across the interval and is evaluated against adapted single-departure approaches on real road networks.

title: Constrained Path Optimization on Time-Dependent Road Networks
label: WISE 2024 · Posters and Demos Track
venue: Web Information Systems Engineering – WISE 2024 PhD Symposium, Demos and Workshops
citation: Lecture Notes in Computer Science 15463, pp. 274–282 (published 2025)
summary: This paper studies how to find loopless routes that maximize preference scores while meeting a travel-time budget in time-dependent road networks. The work explores a broader feasible search space than aggressively pruned alternatives and supports parallel execution. Experiments assess route quality and practical response times on large networks.

title: A Multi-Threading Algorithm for Constrained Path Optimization Problem on Road Networks
citation: Lecture Notes in Computer Science 13724, pp. 110–118 (2022)
summary: This paper addresses routes that maximize a score while remaining within a specified cost budget. The approach broadens the search for promising routes and distributes work across multiple threads to control response time. The evaluation investigates solution quality, workload balance, and how performance changes as additional processing cores become available.

title: NEAT Activity Detection Using Smartwatch at Low Sampling Frequency
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on SmartWorld, Ubiquitous Intelligence & Computing (UIC track)
summary: This paper investigates activity detection from smartwatch signals collected at a low sampling frequency. It examines how a lightweight sensing setup can support recognition of everyday physical activity while reducing the amount of collected data. The work connects wearable sensing, classification, and practical energy-aware monitoring constraints.

title: A Fairness Conscious Cache Replacement Policy for Last Level Cache
venue: Design, Automation and Test in Europe (DATE 2021)
summary: This paper studies cache replacement with fairness among competing workloads in the last-level cache. It considers how replacement decisions can balance performance and shared-resource treatment, and evaluates the policy using system-level cache experiments. The work addresses a computer architecture problem alongside the later focus on graph and data management.

title: CAMOUFLAGE: An Efficient Mechanism to Hide Congestion in NVM LLC
label: HiPC 2023 Student Research Symposium · Extended abstract
citation: Extended abstract in the symposium compendium (2023)
summary: This extended abstract presents CAMOUFLAGE, a mechanism intended to hide congestion effects in a non-volatile-memory last-level cache. It appeared in the HiPC 2023 Student Research Symposium compendium; the linked DOI identifies that compendium rather than an individual CAMOUFLAGE paper.
